paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. It's easy to point at somebody else's mess and feel pretty good about ourselves. Paul says that when we pass judgment and do the same things, we have "no excuse" (Romans 2:1). I've been that stamper hollering about crumbs with crumbs all over my apron.

But God's judgment is not like ours. It is "based on truth" (Romans 2:2), and "God does not show favoritism" (Romans 2:11). Jew or Greek, it makes no difference to Him. Hearing the law isn't enough either, because it is "the doers of the law who will be declared righteous" (Romans 2:13). And when Gentiles, who don't have the law, do by nature what it requires, they show that "the work of the law is written on their hearts" (Romans 2:15).

So what do we do with that? Paul says it plainly: "God's kindness leads you to repentance" (Romans 2:4). God isn't waiting around to catch us. He's patient with us, and that patience is an invitation to turn back to Him. God will judge men's secrets "through Christ Jesus" (Romans 2:16), so my job, and yours, is to stop pointing fingers, let His kindness soften a hard heart, and keep on doing good.
